title: Attack Path Scenario
description: Canonical record for one attack-path scenario. Slides, coverage metrics and tabletop material are all generated FROM this record. This file is the system of record; PowerPoint is a build artifact.

schema_version.description: Bump only on breaking schema change. Migration notes go in schema/CHANGELOG.md.

id.description: Zero-padded scenario number. Immutable once published. Never reused, even after retirement.

slug.description: Stable kebab-case handle used in filenames and cross-references.

title.description: Scenario title as it appears on the slide, without the 'Scenario NN · ' prefix.

one_liner.description: The 'In plain terms' paragraph. Must be readable by a non-specialist executive. No acronyms without expansion.

status.description: retired scenarios stay in the repo forever; they are excluded from current metrics but preserve history.

primary_layer_component.description: Where the scenario primarily operates. Drives the index slide.

priority_rationale.description: Why this priority. Each item must fit one line on the slide (<=130 chars). At least one must reference our own exposure, not just the threat.

mode.description: attack: an adversary drives the chain. failure: no adversary — the chain is failure propagation (a control degrades, a dependency fails, an agent misbehaves without malice). Framework mapping is often thin or empty for failure records and the validator relaxes accordingly; the telemetry map is unchanged and is where all the value sits.

framework_mapping.description: Scenario-level mapping. Step-level mapping lives on attack_path[].

baseline.description: Pointer to frameworks/baseline-YYYY.MM.yaml. Every mapping in this file is expressed in THAT baseline's vocabulary. Never mix baselines within a record.

attack.description: MITRE ATT&CK technique IDs. Ordered as the chain proceeds, not sorted.

atlas.description: MITRE ATLAS technique or tactic IDs.

owasp_llm.description: Edition-qualified, e.g. LLM03:2025. OWASP renumbers between editions; the bare number is meaningless.

owasp_agentic.description: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications, edition-qualified, e.g. ASI01:2026.

mapping_confidence.description: authoritative = the linkage is published by the framework owner (in practice: only ATLAS attack-reference fields qualify). editorial = OUR judgment. Almost every cross-framework mapping is editorial. See docs/03-framework-mapping.md.

mapping_notes.description: Required in practice when mapping_confidence is editorial: state the reasoning and any mapping a reasonable analyst would dispute.

attack_path.description: The ordered chain. Six steps is the slide's hard ceiling. If the chain needs more, the scenario is too broad -- split it.

layer.description: Free-text layer tag shown in brackets on the slide, e.g. 'Data / inbound', 'Host / Cloud'. Kept free-text deliberately -- it is a reading aid, not a controlled field. The controlled field is classification.ai_infrastructure_layer.

text.description: One line. The renderer will not wrap gracefully past ~125 chars including the step prefix and layer tag.

control_held.description: True if a control blocked or degraded this step in the source incident. Recording what HELD is as valuable as recording what failed, and it is the most commonly omitted field.

telemetry.description: Telemetry rows. Every attack_path step must have a matching 'attack-step' row. Additional 'control' rows are allowed for verification/preventive signals. The program's word for this data is evidence; the field name 'telemetry' is kept for compatibility with existing records and consumers.

step.description: Row number as rendered. For kind 'attack-step' this MUST match an attack_path step. For kind 'control' it is display order only. Max 8 so a six-step scenario still has legal numbers for control rows.

kind.description: attack-step: answers a numbered step in attack_path. control: a verification or preventive signal that is not tied to a step (e.g. 'model signature verified at import'). Control rows may carry a row number beyond the step count. Modeling these explicitly stops the validator from reading a deliberate control row as a missing attack step.

signal.description: What is emitted. A noun phrase, not a sentence. Schema hard cap 80; the quality bar prefers a tighter limit (see tools/validate.py LIMITS).

emitted_at.description: Which layer or control emits it. Use ' · ' as the separator, matching the deck. Schema hard cap 90; the quality bar prefers a tighter limit (see tools/validate.py LIMITS).

source.description: The EXACT system this signal comes from, or would come from. The product, log source, index, table, topic or endpoint by name. 'emitted_at' is the category ('EDR / endpoint'); 'source' is the specific thing ('CrowdStrike Falcon ProcessRollup2, index=edr_main'). Required in practice for Have and Collectable: a Have with no named source cannot be verified, and a Collectable with no named source cannot be wired up. For Blind rows, leave empty or state where it would have to come from.

data_components.description: ATT&CK data components (DCxxxx). NOTE: ATT&CK v18 removed data sources and replaced them with data components. Do not use DSxxxx on baselines >= 2025.10.

coverage.description: DERIVED from dettect scores when present -- see docs/04-measurement.md for the derivation. Stored explicitly so the renderer and any offline reader do not need the derivation logic. The validator recomputes it and errors on mismatch.

dettect.description: DeTT&CT scoring. Optional at draft stage, REQUIRED for a scenario to count toward maturity reporting. This is what turns a judgment call into an evidence-backed determination.

visibility.description: DeTT&CT visibility scale. 0 None, 1 Minimal, 2 Medium, 3 Good, 4 Excellent.

detection.description: DeTT&CT detection maturity. -1 None, 0 Forensics/context only, 1 Basic, 2 Fair, 3 Good, 4 Very good, 5 Excellent.

quality.description: The five DeTT&CT data-quality dimensions, each 0-5.

detection_opportunity.description: What you would actually alert on. One line on the slide. Write the OUTCOME to detect, not the tool that detects it. Schema hard cap 130; the quality bar prefers a tighter limit (see tools/validate.py LIMITS).

owner.description: Team accountable for this data source. A Blind row with no owner is an orphan and will never be fixed.

evidence.description: Link or reference proving the coverage assessment -- a query that returns rows, a rule ID, a ticket. Required for any 'Have' claim under the quality bar.

backlog_ref.description: Ticket ID for the instrumentation work, when coverage is Collectable or Blind and the gap has been accepted for work. This field is the closed loop.

notes.description: Row-level working notes captured during a session. Never rendered on the slides.

commentary.description: The three-paragraph analysis block on the telemetry slide.

scaled_up.description: The 'If this scaled up' box. ALWAYS hypothetical -- must not assert anything as observed.

incidents.description: Slugs of records in incidents/. Referential integrity is enforced by the validator.

hardening.description: Remediations ranked by leverage against THIS chain. Optional on the slides, but this is what a tabletop consumes.

breaks_step.description: Which attack_path step(s) this control breaks. A hardening item that breaks no step is generic best practice and does not belong here.

reviewed_by.description: Required before status may become 'published'. Must differ from authored_by.

notes.description: Analyst working notes. Never rendered. Use freely -- disagreements, open questions, things the next author should know.

evidenceTier.description: seen-in-the-wild: it has happened to a real organization. seen-in-research: demonstrated by researchers, not yet in an incident. doomsday: hypothetical worst case, never observed, included as a stress test.

coverage.description: Have: a control already emits this AND it is wired to detection. Collectable: the source exists but is not wired to detection. Blind: nothing produces it today.
